glen_wanderer.text: I came for a picnic and got the best view on Skye. Cone-shaped hills in every direction, and not a soul about. Just you, me, and a sheep with an air of superiority.
My gran said the fairies live under those hills. She said to leave a bit of bread out. I left a sausage roll. It was gone in the morning. Maybe a crow.

then.text: The glen is quiet. A flattened ring in the heather is the size of a very large dog, and the breeze carries a faint, satisfied snuffle.

else.text: The cone-shaped hills lean in. Out of the heather, a shape stands up that was a hill a moment ago: a hound the size of a calf, coat the dark green of wet moss, tail curled up over its back in a plait.
The hound lowers his great head and says, in a voice like a landslide being polite: "Wuf."
The Frost Stone is cold in your pocket and the hound's breath is warm on your hand. It has been waiting here a long time for someone to ask a polite question.

then.text: The Cù-Sìth bumps his enormous head against your hip and follows you out of the heather, green as a hill at dusk, leaving paw prints that are gone by the time you look back. He barks once. You're indoors already.

else.text: The hound vanishes into the heather without bending a stem. A long bark rolls over the hills, a little amused, and the glen is empty. He'll be back if you want to try again.
The glen is hushed, the way a room is hushed when someone has just stopped talking. A cold wind goes through the heather the wrong way.
Far away, down the glen, something barks.
Woof. That is two. It is a good deal closer.

then.text: Three. Exactly three. In the old stories, that is the signal to be indoors. A pause, a gentle rustle in the heather, and the wind turns back the right way, as though someone has been satisfied.

else.text: You count again, and still can't be sure. The wind drops, the heather settles, and something very large chuckles a long way off. It is not unkind, only amused.
Whatever barks in this glen is not ready to be met. The Frost Stone, perhaps. The Keeper in Inverness has the Stone the old stories say he's waiting for.
